name: neq->eq
justification: handleSell declares `let isOnBench = unit !== null;` (line 258, shifted from 254 by the s11 red-team HIGH-1 rng-derived-id fix) but the variable isOnBench is never read anywhere else in the file (verified by grep for 'isOnBench' across preparation/preparation.mjs: the only occurrence is this declaration). The very next statement `if (!unit) { return state; }` makes the same null-check decision independently, without consulting isOnBench. Flipping `!==` to `===` changes the value assigned to isOnBench, but that value has zero effect on control flow, output state, emitted events, or return value. No test can observe the difference because there is nothing downstream to observe. Verified empirically: hand-mutating this line leaves the full suite (84/84, including the new properties.i2.test.mjs Sell-path tests) green.

name: eq->neq
justification: handlePlace's `else if (target_zone === 'bench')` branch (line 515, shifted from 511 by the s11 red-team HIGH-1 rng-derived-id fix) body is exactly `return state;` (line 513), which is byte-for-byte identical to the function's final fallback `return state;` (line 516) reached when neither the 'board' nor the mutated 'bench' condition matches. Tracing both operators for every possible target_zone value once the preceding `target_zone === 'board'` check (line 485) has already failed: with the original `===`, target_zone==='bench' enters the branch and returns the untouched `state`; with the mutant `!==`, target_zone==='bench' skips the branch and falls through to the outer `return state;` instead — same object, same value, same reference. For any other target_zone the two operators trade places on which return statement fires, but both statements return the identical unmodified `state` binding. No test can distinguish because the two code paths are referentially and structurally equivalent (Board->Bench placement is explicitly 'not yet implemented' per the comment on line 512). Verified empirically: hand-mutating this line leaves the full suite (84/84, including the new properties.i2.test.mjs Place-path tests covering 'board', malformed unit_instance_id, and malformed target_zone) green.

name: or->and
justification: handlePlace's entry guard `typeof unit_instance_id !== 'string' || typeof target_zone !== 'string'` (line 473, shifted from 469 by the s11 red-team HIGH-1 rng-derived-id fix) is fully redundant with type-safe handling later in the same function, for BOTH single-condition-true cases (the only cases where || and && diverge): (1) malformed unit_instance_id (any non-string) with valid target_zone: bench.findOnBench(bench, unit_instance_id) (bench/bench.mjs, no type validation on the id parameter) does `bench.find(u => u.unit_instance_id === unit_instance_id) || null` — a strict-equality search that returns null for any type mismatch, and the immediately following `if (!unit) return state;` (line 480-481) rejects deterministically with the identical outcome as the line-469 guard would have produced. (2) valid unit_instance_id with malformed target_zone (any non-string): execution reaches `if (target_zone === 'board')` (line 485) and `else if (target_zone === 'bench')` (line 511), both strict string-literal comparisons that are trivially false for any non-string value (no coercion), falling through to the same final `return state;` (line 516) that line 469's guard would have produced directly. Both single-true branches therefore reach byte-for-byte the same outcome (unchanged state, no events) whether the guard fires early (||) or is skipped and re-derived downstream (&&-mutant behavior). The double-true and double-false cases are identical for || and && by construction, so no input can ever make this mutant observable. Verified empirically: hand-mutating line 469 to && leaves the full suite (85/85, including the properties.i2.test.mjs Place-path tests with malformed unit_instance_id alone and malformed target_zone alone) green.
